title: Nothing Good Happens After 2 A.M.
cn: 第 18 集 · 凌晨两点之后
novel:
Lily had a rule, and she [[warned|warn]] Ted about it often: nothing good ever happens after two in the morning.

That night [[insomnia|insomnia]] kept him awake. The street below was [[deserted|deserted]]; a single [[streetlamp|streetlamp]] buzzed. The whole city had settled into a heavy [[stillness|stillness]].

At 2:07 his phone [[buzzed|buzz]]. A [[murmur|murmur]] of a voice, a girl from long ago, asking to come over.

He knew the [[temptation|temptation]] was a trap. He also knew he had almost no [[self-control|self-control]] left at that hour. [[Drowsy|drowsy]] and warm, he began to [[rationalise|rationalise]] it: they were only going to talk.

Every bad decision needs a good [[excuse|excuse]]. Ted found three.

He stood in the empty [[corridor|corridor]] waiting for the [[doorbell|doorbell]], at a quiet [[crossroads|crossroads]] between the person he was and the person he wanted to be. His [[judgment|judgment]] was gone. Only [[weakness|weakness]] and a soft [[haze|haze]] of hope remained.

He could not [[resist|resist]].

The [[consequence|consequence]] arrived at [[dawn|dawn]], as it always does: grey light, a cold flat, and a slow, [[inevitable|inevitable]] feeling of being [[ashamed|ashamed]].

Lily's rule, it turned out, was science.

warn.en: to tell someone about a danger before it happens

insomnia.en: the problem of not being able to sleep

deserted.en: empty, with no people at all

streetlamp.en: a tall light at the side of a road

buzz.en: to make a low humming sound, like a bee or a phone

murmur.en: a soft, low sound of talking

temptation.en: a strong wish to do something you know is wrong

self-control.en: the power to stop yourself doing what you should not do

rationalise.cn: 为（错事）找理由（美式 rationalize）
rationalise.en: to give clever reasons for something you know is wrong

excuse.en: a reason you give to make a mistake sound acceptable

corridor.en: a long narrow passage inside a building

doorbell.en: the button outside a door that rings inside

crossroads.cn: 十字路口；人生的抉择点
crossroads.en: a point where you must choose which way to go

judgment.en: the ability to make good decisions

weakness.en: a fault in your character that makes you fail

haze.en: thin mist; or a state where you cannot think clearly

resist.en: to stop yourself from doing something you want

consequence.en: what happens as a result of what you did

dawn.en: the time when the sun first comes up

inevitable.en: certain to happen; impossible to stop

ashamed.en: feeling bad because you did something wrong
